title: [Bug] LiteLLM exception when using OpenAI Speech-To-Text models
author: LizardBlizzard

comments.author: TomeHirata
comments.body: Does it work when you use `gpt-4o-mini`?

comments.author: LizardBlizzard
akshatvishu
comments.body:
Hey @LizardBlizzard ! I think   ` model="gpt-4o-mini-transcribe"` use `v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint as mentioned in the [open ai docs](<https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/gpt-4o-transcribe>) and currently `dspy` only supports   `model_type: Literal['chat', 'text', 'responses']`  , please correct me if I am wrong!

`ref`: <https://dspy.ai/api/models/LM/>, 


As for the `x-wav` error when you  do `Using DSPy with gpt-4o-mini instead`, I think this is a bug in the codebase (happy to contribute towards a fix! ) which arises at  https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/9dafdcc7b1f80a3fa875d2abdc55197183015489/dspy/adapters/types/audio.py#L82
```
audio_format = mime_type.split("/")[1]  # → 'x-wav'
```
and that value 'x-wav' is later rejected by OpenAI’s API (since it the valid accepted format is `wav`). Thus, what you can do for now is try to bypass this by:
```py
import base64
from pathlib import Path
import dspy

class TranscribeSignature(dspy.Signature):
    """Transcribe the given audio file into text."""
    audio: dspy.Audio = dspy.InputField()
    transcription: str = dspy.OutputField()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    audio_path = Path("xyz.wav") 

    if not audio_path.exists():
        print(f"Error: Audio file not found at {audio_path}")
    else:
        #  Read the audio file as raw bytes
        with audio_path.open("rb") as f:
            audio_bytes = f.read()
        
        # Manually base64 encode the bytes
        b64_data = base64.b64encode(audio_bytes).decode("utf-8")
        
        # Explicitly construct the Audio object, forcing the
        # OpenAI-supported format "wav" to bypass the 'x-wav' bug.
        audio = dspy.Audio(data=b64_data, audio_format="wav")

        # Now, call `gpt-4o-mini` as mentioned by Tome !
        lm = dspy.LM(model="gpt-4o-mini")
        dspy.settings.configure(lm=lm)

        transcriber = dspy.Predict(TranscribeSignature)

        response = transcriber(audio=audio)
        
        print("Transcription:")
        print(response.transcription)
```

comments.author: akshatvishu
comments.body:
Hey @TomeHirata  , the `mimetypes.guess_type()` is used internally at [adapters/types/audio.py](github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/9dafdcc7b1f80a3fa875d2abdc55197183015489/dspy/adapters/types/audio.py#L75) , but it cannot recognize file extensions other than conventional one and should be patched with something like:

```py
# In dspy/adapters/audio.py

MIME_TYPE_MAP = {
    "x-wav": "wav",

}

@classmethod
    def from_file(cls, file_path: str) -> "Audio":
        """
        Read local audio file and encode it as base64.
        """
        if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
            raise ValueError(f"File not found: {file_path}")

        mime_type, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(file_path)
        if not mime_type or not mime_type.startswith("audio/"):
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MIME type for audio: {mime_type}")

        with open(file_path, "rb") as file:
            file_data = file.read()

        audio_format = mime_type.split("/")[1]

        # Normalize the audio format
        audio_format = MIME_TYPE_MAP.get(audio_format, audio_format)   # Apply fix here

        
        encoded_data = base64.b64encode(file_data).decode("utf-8")
        return cls(data=encoded_data, audio_format=audio_format)
```
same fix for `def from_url` and `def encode_audio`

I also checked for the following types:
```py
MIME_TYPE_MAP = {
    "x-wav": "wav",
    "x-flac": "flac",
    "x-m4a": "m4a",
    "mpga": "mp3",
}
```
and only `x-wav` throws error thus, we can also move the correction logic inside each fn :

```
@classmethod
    def from_file(cls, file_path: str) -> "Audio":
        """
        Read local audio file and encode it as base64.
        """
        if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
            raise ValueError(f"File not found: {file_path}")

        mime_type, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(file_path)
        if not mime_type or not mime_type.startswith("audio/"):
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MIME type for audio: {mime_type}")

        with open(file_path, "rb") as file:
            file_data = file.read()

        audio_format = mime_type.split("/")[1]

        # This fixes the bug where mimetypes incorrectly guesses "x-wav",
        # ensuring an API-compliant format is used.
        if audio_format == "x-wav":    # fix
            audio_format = "wav"

        
        encoded_data = base64.b64encode(file_data).decode("utf-8")
        return cls(data=encoded_data, audio_format=audio_format)
```
same fix for `def from_url` and `def encode_audio`.

comments.body:
Hey @TomeHirata ,I just opened a PR for this! 

Also, on a side note, I think we should update `CONTRIBUTING.md` to mention that contributors need` Python 3.10` installed for `pre-commit` hooks to work properly.

The issue: 

Current  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` specifies :

```yaml
default_language_version:
  python: python3.10
```
But the current default setup instructions install `Python 3.11` (via either `uv sync` or `conda create -n dspy-dev python=3.11`). This causes `pre-commit` to fail with a`failed to find interpreter for python3.10` error when contributors try to commit. Very trivial matter but I think it will be beneficial for everyone if this info is mentioned upfront . I'm happy to open a separate PR for this documentation fix if you agree!

comments.author: TomeHirata
comments.body: @LizardBlizzard We basically support any OpenAI models that can be called using chat completion endpoint. The 4o transcribe model doesn't support chat completion endpoint (https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/gpt-4o-transcribe), which is why you faced the error. You can either 1) implement your own dspy.LM class that calls the transcription endpoint or 2) file a PR to LiteLLM (instead of DSPy) to support the transcription endpoint from `litellm.completion`.
